data.narrative:
Captura is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Harry Atwater and CX Xiang that has raised $30M+. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA), with notable private-stage companies including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Our valuation relies on stage-progression methodology, as a peer-median approach cannot be applied. The Climate & Energy sector lacks a sufficient narrow-stage peer set—despite 9 same-sector companies in our universe, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparables yielded fewer than 3 datapoints, making sector-specific multiples unreliable. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $30M total raised proxy, a typical progression coefficient from Series A to later stages, implying a post-money valuation of $60M.

The triangulated valuation range is $51M to $69M, with a median of $60M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty: the analysis lacks corroborating multiples from same-stage peers and cannot benchmark against sector-specific revenue or EBITDA metrics due to data constraints. Key variables affecting valuation include revenue traction, technology maturation, and capital efficiency relative to the broader frontier-tech cohort. Additional peer data or financial metrics would improve conviction in this range.
